title: Endpoint DLP: what Microsoft Purview enforces on onboarded devices
summary: The page passes: Microsoft documentation supports its controls, licensing and device-protection claims. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting macOS support wording, restore omitted policy-wizard headings and cite the source for the Power Platform comparison.

claims.where: title; summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP extends Microsoft Purview DLP to monitoring and restricting sensitive-file activity on onboarded devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices, and Windows certain server versions.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices.
claims.quote: Microsoft Endpoint DLP allows you to monitor onboarded Windows 10, and Windows 11 and onboarded macOS devices running any of the three latest released versions.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP overview describes macOS support as the three latest released major versions.
claims.quote: macOS (the three latest released major versions)
claims.fix: After the platform-support sentence, add: 'The Purview service description instead lists macOS Catalina 10.15 and higher.' The conflicting wording is at https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-data-loss-prevention-endpoint-data-loss-protection-dlp.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports certain Windows Server versions.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP allows you to onboard devices running Windows Server 2019 and later versions.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is a different mechanism from Power Platform data policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention to sources for the comparison with connector-governing Power Platform data policies. Retain the cited Endpoint DLP overview for device-file protection.

claims.where: What it is: Onboarding; controls[2]; What to check
claims.claim: A device must be onboarded before Endpoint DLP can monitor and protect sensitive items on it.
claims.quote: You must enable device monitoring and onboard your endpoints before you can monitor and protect sensitive items on a device.

claims.claim: Device onboarding is shared with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
claims.quote: Device onboarding is shared across Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE).

claims.claim: Onboarding a device in the Microsoft Purview portal also onboards it into MDE.
claims.quote: Onboarding devices in Microsoft Purview portal also onboards them into MDE.

claims.where: What it is: Onboarding; What to check
claims.claim: Windows devices must be Microsoft Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered.
claims.quote: All devices must be one of these: Microsoft Entra joined; Microsoft Entra hybrid joined; Microsoft Entra registered

claims.claim: Windows device preparation requires Real-time protection to be enabled.
claims.quote: None of Windows Security components need to be active, but the Real-time protection and Behavior monitor must be enabled.

claims.claim: Windows device preparation requires Behavior monitor to be enabled.
claims.quote: None of Windows Security components need to be active, but the Real-time protection and Behavior monitor must be enabled.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified
claims.claim: On Windows 10/11 and macOS, file creation triggers a full scan for sensitive information types and labels.
claims.quote: Creation or Modification: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified
claims.claim: On Windows 10/11 and macOS, file modification triggers a full scan for sensitive information types and labels.
claims.quote: Creation or Modification: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified
claims.claim: Reading an already classified file triggers policy re-evaluation if policies, rules or sensitive information types changed.
claims.quote: When an already classified file is read, Endpoint DLP checks for any changes to the policies, rules, or SITs. If there is a change in the DLP configuration, it re-evaluates the policies and rules, but it will not re-extract the text.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Policies; controls[0].note; Governance controls: interaction; What to check
claims.claim: A Devices-location policy is enforced only when both the user and device are in scope.
claims.quote: For a DLP policy to be enforced on an endpoint, both the user and the device must be included in the policy scope.

claims.claim: A device needs access to all Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: Therefore, the device must have access to all endpoint DLP policies in order to evaluate items.

claims.claim: A device can have multiple users whose scoped policies differ.
claims.quote: A device can support multiple user accounts. Because endpoint policies are scoped to users, different users of the device may have different policies scoped to them.

claims.where: What it is: Endpoint settings; controls[1]; Governance controls: interaction
claims.claim: Centrally configured Endpoint settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can audit or restrict copying sensitive files to USB removable media.
claims.quote: Copy to USB removable device | When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can audit or restrict copying sensitive files to network shares.
claims.quote: Copy to a network share | When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to any network share

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can audit or restrict printing sensitive files.
claims.quote: Print | When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the printing of protected files from an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can audit or restrict copying protected file content to the clipboard.
claims.quote: When a user attempts to copy content from a protected file, you can block, block with override, or audit the copying of protected files to a clipboard on an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP rules can audit or restrict uploading protected files to restricted cloud service domains.
claims.quote: You can block, warn, or audit when protected files can be uploaded or prevented from being uploaded to cloud services based on the allow/unallowed domains list in Data loss prevention settings.

claims.claim: Copy or move using RDP is not supported on macOS.
claims.quote: Copy or move using RDP | Detects when a user attempts to copy an item to a remote desktop session. | Supported | Supported | Not supported | Auditable and restrictable

claims.claim: JIT protection can block egress on monitored files that have not been evaluated while policy evaluation completes.
claims.quote: JIT candidate file: Files that DLP hasn't evaluated or that have a stale classification.

claims.claim: JIT protection can also block egress on files whose classification is stale.
claims.quote: A user attempts an egress activity on an item that has never been classified or that is classified with a stale policy.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on whether the user is in JIT scope.
claims.quote: JIT protection blocks the egress activity when all the following conditions are true: ... The user is in the scope of JIT.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on DLP policies defining Block or Block with override for the attempted activity.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies exist that block or block with override for the egress activity.

claims.claim: JIT blocking depends on whether the destination is allowed.
claims.quote: The egress activity isn't to an allowed location. For example, an allowed printer, USB device, URL, or network share.

claims.claim: JIT blocking behaviour depends on pause and resume support.
claims.quote: For all the items that didn't complete DLP policy evaluation within three seconds OR don't support resume, JIT evaluation allows two more seconds.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: Policy updates made while a Windows device is offline are not pushed to that device until it is online.
claims.quote: Policies that are updated while a device is offline won't be pushed to that device. Similarly, such policies won't be enforced on that device, until the device is back online.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices
claims.claim: Policy changes reach a previously offline Windows device after it reconnects.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Offline Windows devices

claims.claim: Onboarding devices enables automatic auditing of Office, PDF and CSV file activity by default.

claims.claim: With Always audit file activity for devices enabled, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and CSV activity is audited even without a targeting policy.
claims.quote: If the Always audit file activity for devices setting is on, activities on any Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and .csv files are always audited, even if the device isn't targeted by any policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: interaction
claims.claim: Always audit file activity for devices can be turned off to limit auditing to policy-related activity.
claims.quote: If you only want to monitor data from policy matches, you can turn off the Always audit file activity for devices in the Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings.

claims.claim: Onboarded devices can report audit activity to Activity explorer before a policy exists.
claims.quote: By default, when you onboard devices, the system automatically audits activity for Office, PDF, and CSV files. You can review this activity in activity explorer.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Users; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that targeting devices whose users do not meet required criteria can cause unintended enforcement and instructs explicit exclusions.
claims.quote: If a policy is scoped to devices where the signed-in users do not meet the required criteria, ensure those users or devices or both are explicitly excluded from the policy. Failure to do so may lead to unintended policy enforcement behavior.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Excluded paths; What to check

claims.claim: Exceeding a configured advanced-classification bandwidth limit stops user content being sent to the cloud.
claims.quote: If you set a bandwidth usage limit and that usage limit is exceeded, DLP stops sending the user content to the cloud.

claims.claim: Exact data match, named entities, trainable classifiers and credential classifiers are unavailable while advanced classification is bandwidth-limited.
claims.quote: At that point, data classification continues locally on the device but classification by using exact data match, named entities, trainable classifiers, and credential classifiers isn't available.

claims.claim: Cloud advanced classification resumes when bandwidth usage drops below the configured limit.

claims.claim: Advanced classification does not scan text files larger than 64 MB.
claims.quote: Advanced classification doesn't work for text files larger than 64 MB, even if you set the bandwidth limit to Do not limit bandwidth. Unlimited.
